name: Scrollbar
author: Themepoints

sections.description:
Scrollbar lets you restyle the scrollbar on your whole site and see the result live while you edit. Pick a preset, adjust the colors and shape, and save.

Two engines

  • Native CSS (default for new installs). Pure CSS. No JavaScript, no extra library, and visitors keep normal keyboard, touch and screen reader scrolling.
  • Advanced (jQuery). Smooth scrolling, auto-hide, left or right rail and an optional horizontal bar, powered by nicescroll 3.7.6.

Features

  • Live preview with light and dark views on the settings page.
  • 8 ready-made presets.
  • Thumb color, hover color, track color, opacity, width, corner radius, border width, style and color.
  • Dark mode colors that follow the visitor’s color scheme.
  • Hide on small screens, skip chosen posts or pages, skip chosen user roles.
  • Style extra scrollable areas with your own CSS selectors.
  • Scroll Box block and [scrollbar] shortcode for fixed-height scrolling content.
  • Optional reading progress bar and back-to-top button.
  • Respects the visitor’s “reduce motion” setting in Advanced mode.
  • Import, export and reset your settings.
  • Settings screen loads its assets only on its own page.

Browser note

Full styling (width, corners, borders) works in Chrome, Edge, Safari and other WebKit/Blink browsers. Firefox supports a thumb color, track color and thin or regular width through its own scrollbar properties. The Advanced engine draws its own scrollbar and looks the same in all browsers.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/scrollbar/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > Scrollbar and choose your style.
sections.faq:
Which engine should I use?

Start with Native CSS. It is the lightest and the most accessible. Choose Advanced only if you want smooth scrolling, auto-hide, a left-side scrollbar or a horizontal bar.

I updated from version 2.x. Did my settings change?

No. Your saved color, width, radius, border, speed and auto-hide values are imported and the Advanced engine stays selected, so your site looks the same. You can switch to Native CSS at any time.

How do I add a scrolling box inside a post?

In the block editor add the Scroll Box block. Anywhere else use [scrollbar height="300px"]Your content[/scrollbar].

How do I turn the scrollbar off on one page?

Go to Settings > Scrollbar > General and add the page ID under “Skip these posts or pages”.

The scrollbar is hidden behind my sticky header.

Use the Advanced engine and raise the Layer (z-index) value on the Behavior tab.

Can developers disable it conditionally?

Yes. Use the scrollbar_wp_should_load filter and return false.
sections.changelog:
3.0.0

  • New: Native CSS engine with no JavaScript or jQuery, now the default for new installs. Existing sites stay on the Advanced engine.
  • New: Redesigned settings page with tabs, live light/dark preview and 8 presets.
  • New: Track color, hover color, opacity, border color and border style.
  • New: Dark mode colors.
  • New: Left or right scrollbar, horizontal bar and z-index controls (Advanced engine).
  • New: Hide on small screens, skip posts, pages and user roles, and style extra CSS selectors.
  • New: Scroll Box block and [scrollbar] shortcode.
  • New: Reading progress bar and back-to-top button.
  • New: Import, export and reset.
  • New: Settings link on the Plugins screen and the scrollbar_wp_should_load filter.
  • Improved: All options are stored in one validated settings array and saved through the WordPress Settings API.
  • Improved: Values are range-checked and invalid colors fall back to defaults.
  • Improved: Frontend script is loaded in the footer with the correct nicescroll version and an inline config added through wp_add_inline_script.
  • Improved: Admin scripts and styles load only on the Scrollbar settings page.
  • Improved: Advanced engine respects the visitor’s reduced-motion preference.
  • Fixed: Settings screen defaults now match what visitors see on the site.
  • Fixed: PHP syntax that caused a fatal error on PHP older than 7.3.
  • Fixed: Missing uninstall cleanup. Options are now removed when the plugin is deleted.
  • Removed: The red “Donate!” link in the Plugins list and the empty color-picker script.

2.0.9

  • Security Enhancement: Implemented rigorous nonce verification (wp_nonce_field and wp_verify_nonce) across the settings form to fully protect against CSRF vulnerabilities.
  • WordPress Coding Standards: Added strict sanitization callbacks (sanitize_hex_color, absint, and custom boolean validation) to all register_setting() calls, resolving all Plugin Check validation errors.
  • Asset Loading Optimization: Refactored admin script and style enqueuing to load the WordPress color picker strictly on the plugin’s dedicated settings page (admin_enqueue_scripts), preventing global script conflicts.
  • Form & Capability Hardening: Added explicit capability checks (current_user_can('manage_options')) and robust handling for $_POST array indices to prevent undefined notices and secure data processing.
  • UI Refinements: Streamlined markup in the admin options template and updated the JavaScript initialization to ensure secure attribute escaping and reliable rendering.
